chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated, saying: Some of our companions narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Ayyub ibn Noah, who said: I said to Abul Hasan ar-Rida (peace be upon him):

"We hope that you are the master of this matter and that Allah may pave the way to you peacefully and without a sword. Homage has been paid to you, and coins have been struck with your name." He said: "None of us to whom letters were sent, who was pointed at with fingers, who was asked about religious matters, and to whom wealth was sent, was assassinated or died in his bed, until Allah sends for this matter a young man from us whose birth and upbringing were hidden, but his lineage is not hidden."
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the hidden birth and lineage of the Mahdi in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the pattern of public Imams being either martyred or dying in relative obscurity will culminate in a final Imam whose initial concealment (ghaybah) is profound yet whose lineage remains undisputed. This hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* establishes the theological basis for the Major Occultation, distinguishing the hidden Imam from his predecessors who were more visibly active in public affairs.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (9) Muhammad bin Ya’qoob narrated from some of his companions from Sa’d bin Abdullah that Ayyoob bin Noah had said: “I said to Abul Hasan ar-Redha (as):

“We hope that you are the man of the matter and that Allah may pave the way to you peacefully and without fighting. Homage has been paid to you and money is coined with your name.” He said: “None of us that letters has been sent to, has been pointed at with fingers, has been asked about religious matters and monies (legal religious rights) have been sent to, unless he is killed or he dies in his bed until Allah will send for this matter a boy from our progeny, whose birth and early life will be unknown but his lineage will be not unknown.”
